title: Abortion and mental health, with Antonia Biggs, PhD

sentences.en: In May, a leaked draft of a Supreme Court decision indicated that the court might soon overturn 50 years of legal precedent and strike down Roe v.
sentences.zh: 今年5月，一份泄露的最高法院裁决草案显示，法院可能很快会推翻50年来的法律先例，并推翻“罗诉韦德案”。

sentences.en: Wade, the 1973 ruling that found there is a constitutional right to abortion.
sentences.zh: 该案是1973年的一项裁决，确立了宪法赋予的堕胎权。

sentences.en: Dozens of states are poised to outlaw or dramatically restrict abortion if Roe is overturned.
sentences.zh: 如果“罗诉韦德案”被推翻，数十个州准备取缔或大幅限制堕胎。

sentences.en: While the court has yet to issue a final ruling, we're going to talk today about one aspect of what a post-Roe future would look like.
sentences.zh: 虽然法院尚未发布最终裁决，但我们今天将讨论“后罗诉韦德时代”未来可能的样子。

sentences.en: What could happen to the mental health and well-being of people who are no longer able to access abortion?
sentences.zh: 对于那些无法再进行堕胎的人来说，他们的心理健康和福祉会发生什么？

sentences.en: Abortion opponents have long argued that the procedure harms women's mental health and that it leads to depression, anxiety, regret, and even post-traumatic stress disorder.
sentences.zh: 堕胎反对者长期以来一直认为，堕胎手术会损害女性的心理健康，并导致抑郁、焦虑、后悔，甚至创伤后应激障碍。

sentences.en: But years of research have failed to find that abortion itself causes these outcomes.
sentences.zh: 但多年的研究未能发现堕胎本身会导致这些后果。

sentences.en: So how does obtaining an abortion or being denied one affect mental health and well-being?
sentences.zh: 那么，进行堕胎或被拒绝堕胎如何影响心理健康和福祉？

sentences.en: What are the effects of laws that limit access to abortion, such as those that mandate waiting periods or pre-abortion counseling?
sentences.zh: 限制堕胎途径的法律（例如强制等待期或堕胎前咨询）会产生什么影响？

sentences.en: And how might new laws that outlaw abortion affect people, even in parts of the country where abortion remains legal?
sentences.zh: 即使在堕胎仍然合法的地区，新的堕胎禁令又会如何影响人们？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Antonia Biggs, a social psychologist and associate professor at the Advancing New Standards in Reproductive Health
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是安东尼娅·比格斯博士，她是社会心理学家，也是加州大学旧金山分校“推进生殖健康新标准”项目的副教授。

sentences.en: program at the University of California, San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 项目。

sentences.en: Dr. Biggs studies the mental health effects of abortion.
sentences.zh: 比格斯博士研究堕胎对心理健康的影响。

sentences.en: She led the mental health analysis for the Turnaway Study, a nationwide examination of the health and well-being of women who seek abortions.
sentences.zh: 她领导了“拒绝研究”（Turnaway Study）的心理健康分析，这是一项针对寻求堕胎女性的健康和福祉的全国性调查。

sentences.en: She also researches the challenges people face when accessing sexual and reproductive health services, as well as public attitudes toward
sentences.zh: 她还研究人们在获取性和生殖健康服务时面临的挑战，以及公众对堕胎的态度，

sentences.en: abortion, particularly medication-induced abortion.
sentences.zh: 特别是药物流产的态度。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me, Dr. Biggs.
sentences.zh: 感谢您参加我们的节目，比格斯博士。

sentences.en: Hi, thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 你好，非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: So, so excited to be here.
sentences.zh: 我非常高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: As I mentioned a moment ago, abortion opponents often argue that abortion is in itself bad for people's mental health and can lead to many negative mental health outcomes.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才提到的，堕胎反对者经常辩称，堕胎本身对人们的心理健康有害，并可能导致许多负面的心理健康后果。

sentences.en: The Turnaway Study, on which you worked, addressed this question directly.
sentences.zh: 您参与的“拒绝研究”直接回应了这个问题。

sentences.en: Would you start by telling us about that study, how it was conducted, and what it found?
sentences.zh: 您能先给我们介绍一下这项研究、它是如何进行的以及发现了什么吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So, the Turnaway Study is a national study that was led by my colleague, Dr. Diana Green Foster at ECSF.
sentences.zh: “拒绝研究”是一项由我的同事、加州大学旧金山分校的戴安娜·格林·福斯特博士领导的全国性研究。

sentences.en: And in this study, the impetus behind this study really came from this idea that abortion harms women's mental health.
sentences.zh: 这项研究背后的推动力实际上源于一种观点，即堕胎会损害女性的心理健康。

sentences.en: This is something that
sentences.zh: 这是肯尼迪大法官在“冈萨雷斯诉卡哈特案”中提到的观点，

sentences.en: Justice Kennedy had stated in the Gonzalez v.
sentences.zh: 他在该案中明确表示，虽然我们没有可靠的数据来衡量这种现象，但得出以下结论似乎并不例外：

sentences.en: Carhart case, where he literally said that we don't have reliable data to measure the phenomenon, but that it seems unexceptional to conclude that some women
sentences.zh: 一些女性会为自己的堕胎感到后悔，随后会出现严重的抑郁和自卑感。

sentences.en: come to regret their abortion and that severe depression and low self-esteem is going to follow.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一个被纳入许多州级堕胎限制中的假设，尽管他清楚地说明我们没有可靠的数据。

sentences.en: So, this is an assumption that has been integrated in a lot of the state-level restrictions on abortion, yet he clearly states that we don't have reliable data.
sentences.zh: 所以，“拒绝研究”确实旨在提供这些可靠的数据。

sentences.en: So, the Turnaway Study really aimed to provide that reliable data.
sentences.zh: 它是我们研究该问题最严谨的研究之一。

sentences.en: So, it's one of the most rigorous studies that we have studying that question.
sentences.zh: 我们招募了近1000名女性并对她们进行了五年的跟踪调查，我们将那些进行了堕胎的人与那些因刚好超过医疗机构孕周限制而被拒绝堕胎的人进行了比较。

sentences.en: So, we recruited nearly 1,000 women and followed them for five years, and we compared people who had
sentences.zh: 我们在全美范围内招募了参与者，并确实能够评估那些进行堕胎的人与被拒绝堕胎的人相比，出现负面心理健康后果的风险是否增加。

sentences.en: an abortion to people who were denied an abortion because they were just above a facility's gestational age limit.
sentences.zh: 我们发现这个假设是错误的，我们发现进行堕胎的人并没有增加出现抑郁、焦虑、自杀意念或创伤后应激障碍的风险。

sentences.en: And we recruited people across the U.S., and we were really able to assess whether the
sentences.zh: 我们观察了所有这些结果，并没有发现堕胎女性的风险有所增加。

sentences.en: people who had an abortion were at increased risk of having negative mental health outcomes when compared to the people who were denied an abortion.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实发现，与能够进行预期堕胎的女性相比，被拒绝堕胎的女性在短期内确实有更高的压力、焦虑、生活满意度低和自卑感。

sentences.en: And what we found is that this assumption is wrong, that we found that people who had an abortion were at no, they were not at an increased
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们发现的结果与人们假设的恰恰相反。

sentences.en: risk of experiencing depression, anxiety, suicidal ideation, post-traumatic stress disorder.
sentences.zh: 另一件事我们发现，大多数女性并不后悔堕胎。

sentences.en: So, we looked at all of those outcomes, and we did not find an increased risk among the women who had an abortion.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们发现近99%的女性在五年多的跟踪调查中表示，堕胎对她们来说是正确的决定。

sentences.en: But what we did find is that the women who were denied an abortion did have short-term elevated levels of stress, anxiety, low life satisfaction, and low self-esteem when compared
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: to the women who were able to get their wanted abortion.
sentences.zh: 您是一位心理学家，在分析“拒绝研究”数据时专注于心理健康结果。

sentences.en: So, in fact, we found the opposite of what people were assuming.
sentences.zh: 但该研究还考察了其他结果，如身体健康以及进行或被拒绝堕胎的经济影响。

sentences.en: And then the other thing we found is that women, most women do not regret their abortion.
sentences.zh: 这些发现中有哪些亮点？

sentences.en: Actually, we found that nearly 99% of women, when we follow them for over five years, say that the abortion was the right decision for them.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 当我们观察所有其他结果时，我们发现被拒绝堕胎的人更有可能经历持续多年的经济困难和经济不安全感。

sentences.en: So, you're a psychologist, and you focused on the mental health outcomes in the analyses of the turnaway data.
sentences.zh: 这影响了被拒绝堕胎者的财务状况，以及他们的孩子和家庭。

sentences.en: But the study also looked at other outcomes like physical health and the economic effects of getting or being denied an abortion.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们更有可能生活在贫困中。

sentences.en: What were some of the highlights of those findings?
sentences.zh: 我们还发现，经历亲密伴侣暴力的人在多年后更有可能被束缚在这些伴侣身边。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 与能够进行堕胎的人相比，被拒绝堕胎的人更有可能与那些暴力的伴侣保持联系。

sentences.en: So, what we found when we look at all the other outcomes that we looked at, we found that the
sentences.zh: 从身体健康的角度来看，我们也知道堕胎比分娩安全得多。

sentences.en: people who were denying abortion were much more likely to experience economic hardship and economic insecurity that lasted for years.
sentences.zh: 在“拒绝研究”中，我们发现被拒绝堕胎并足月分娩的人更有可能出现高血压和慢性疼痛。

sentences.en: This impacted the financial well-being of the people who were denying abortion as well as their children and families.
sentences.zh: 与那些接受了堕胎的人相比，她们健康状况不佳的可能性更大。

sentences.en: So, they were much more likely to live in poverty.
sentences.zh: 最悲惨的是，在被拒绝堕胎的女性中，实际上有两人死于分娩。

sentences.en: We also found that people who were experiencing intimate partner violence were significantly more likely to be tethered to those partners over years.
sentences.zh: 考虑到我们研究中包含的人数，这是一个非常惊人的数字。

sentences.en: The people who were denying abortion were more likely to stay in contact with those violent partners than the people who were able to get their
sentences.zh: 而进行堕胎的人中没有人死亡。

sentences.en: abortions.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们发现这对她们的身体健康造成了非常严重的后果。

sentences.en: And then from a physical health perspective, we also, we know that abortion is much safer than childbirth.
sentences.zh: 进行这类研究最大的挑战是什么？

sentences.en: And in the turnaway study, we found that people who were denied an abortion and carried those pregnancies to term were much more likely to experience hypertension, chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 收集样本困难吗？

sentences.en: They had a greater likelihood of poor health compared to those who have received an abortion.
sentences.zh: 以一种能得到你所需要的方式来构建问题是否困难？

sentences.en: And then most tragically, we actually had two people who died in childbirth of the women who were denied abortion.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲吧。

sentences.en: And that was really an astronomical number when you think of the number of people that we included in this study.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为在“拒绝研究”之前我们没有好的数据，原因之一就是进行这类研究的挑战。

sentences.en: And nobody who had an abortion died.
sentences.zh: 出于显而易见的原因，你不能在伦理上将人们随机分配到堕胎组或非堕胎组。

sentences.en: So, we found, you know, very severe consequences to their physical health.
sentences.zh: 因此，这导致了许多相关性研究，这些研究没有考虑到一些可能使人们容易产生负面心理健康后果的重要因素。

sentences.en: What are the biggest challenges of doing this type of research?
sentences.zh: 这项研究的独特之处在于，我的同事戴安娜·格林·福斯特博士有足够的勇气去做没人认为她能做到的研究，即在人们被拒绝堕胎时采访她们。

sentences.en: Was it hard to collect the sample?
sentences.zh: 所以，人们认为她做不到，但在协助招募的优秀诊所的帮助下，她做到了。

sentences.en: Was it difficult to structure the questions in a way that would get you what you needed?
sentences.zh: 这个想法是由我的一位临床医生同事埃莉诺·德雷博士提出的，她知道女性被拒绝堕胎，并想知道这些人的遭遇。

sentences.en: Tell us about that.
sentences.zh: 这促成了研究设计，并且涉及了所有协助招募的诊所，工作量巨大。

sentences.en: Well, I think that one of the reasons why we haven't had good data up until the turnaway study is because of the challenges conducting this kind of research.
sentences.zh: 然后，我们对人们进行了五年的跟踪调查，每六个月采访一次。

sentences.en: So, you can't randomize people to an abortion group or not abortion group ethically for obvious reasons.
sentences.zh: 总共11轮采访。

sentences.en: And so, that has led to a lot of correlational studies that don't take into account some important factors that could predispose people to negative mental health outcomes.
sentences.zh: 这是一项极其巨大的工作，涉及一个由专家、临床医生、人口统计学家和流行病学家组成的多学科团队。

sentences.en: So, what was unique about this study is that my colleague, Dr. Diana Green Foster, was brave enough
sentences.zh: 这是这项研究的优势之一，但也是一项具有挑战性的研究。

sentences.en: to do the study that nobody thought she could do, which is to interview people who are denied an abortion at the time of being denied an abortion.
sentences.zh: 有什么局限性吗？

sentences.en: So, people didn't think that she could do it, but she did with the help of amazing clinics who helped with the recruitment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你能进行一项没有局限性的理想研究。

sentences.en: It was that the idea was spawned by a colleague of mine who's a clinician, Dr. Eleanor Dre, who knew that women were being turned away and was wanting to know
sentences.zh: 与你必须做的事情相比，它会是什么样子？

sentences.en: what happens to those people.
sentences.zh: 每项研究都有其局限性。

sentences.en: So, that prompted the study design and it was a tremendous amount of work involved all the clinics who helped to recruit.
sentences.zh: 我认为就这种特定的研究设计而言，它是最好的之一。它利用了一种准实验设计。

sentences.en: And then, we followed people for five years interviewing them every six months.
sentences.zh: 局限性之一是参与的人数更多。

sentences.en: So, 11 waves of interviews.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的参与度，理想情况下，你希望每个人都参与。

sentences.en: So, it was a huge, tremendous amount of work and involved a multidisciplinary team of experts, clinicians, demographers, epidemiologists.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这永远是不可能的。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，除了让更多人参与之外，我不确定我们会做些什么不同的事情。

sentences.en: which is one of the strengths of this study, but also a challenging study to conduct.
sentences.zh: 回顾过去，我想我们可能会对调查工具进行一些微调。

sentences.en: What were the limitations?
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，我认为这是一项我们都引以为豪的研究。

sentences.en: I mean, if you could have done, you know, an ideal study with no limitations.
sentences.zh: 堕胎反对者经常引用另一个观点，即许多女性对堕胎感到后悔。

sentences.en: What would it have looked like compared to what you had to do?
sentences.zh: 研究对堕胎和后悔有什么说法？

sentences.en: So, every study has its limitations.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，嗯，“拒绝研究”的研究表明，大多数人并不后悔堕胎。

sentences.en: I think in terms of this particular study design, I think it's one of the beSt. It sort of takes advantage of a quasi-experimental design.
sentences.zh: 99%的女性表示堕胎对她们来说是正确的决定。

sentences.en: One of the limitations is that more people did participate.
sentences.zh: 这种情况持续了五年。

sentences.en: So, our participation, you know, ideally, you want everyone to participate.
sentences.zh: 我们还有来自其他研究的研究，这些研究观察了女性。

sentences.en: But of course, that's never going to be possible.
sentences.zh: 我的同事卡特里娜·坎波特博士采访了一些人，她们说自己有情绪波动，专门试图找到可能对堕胎感到后悔的人。

sentences.en: So, I'm not sure what we would have done differently other than in terms of getting more people to participate.
sentences.zh: 找到这些人非常困难。

sentences.en: I think in retrospect, we would have, we, you know, there's probably like tweaks that we would have done to our survey instruments.
sentences.zh: 但当她找到时，她进行了我想是17次采访。

sentences.en: But in overall, I think it's a study that we're all very proud of.
sentences.zh: 她发现人们后悔的并不是堕胎本身。

sentences.en: There's another idea that's often cited by abortion opponents that many women come to regret having had an abortion.
sentences.zh: 而是人们后悔堕胎周围的环境。

sentences.en: What does the research say about abortion and regret?
sentences.zh: 所以，这被称为决策后悔与情境后悔，这是我的同事凯蒂·沃森写的一篇论文中的术语。

sentences.en: So, the research says that, well, the turnaway study research says that most people do not regret their abortions.
sentences.zh: 其核心思想是，在堕胎的情况下，你希望自己没有处于导致你需要堕胎的那种境地。

sentences.en: 99% of women say that the abortion was the right decision for them.
sentences.zh: 你希望你的伴侣反应不同，更支持你，或者你希望你有更好的经济条件，或者你有更稳定的住房。

sentences.en: And this continues over five years.
sentences.zh: 你生活中有些情况是你希望不同的，这样你就可以足月分娩。

sentences.en: We also have research from other studies
sentences.zh: 所以，人们对这些感到后悔。

sentences.en: that have looked at women.
sentences.zh: 实际上，一旦人们别无选择，很少有人会后悔自己真的进行了堕胎。

sentences.en: So, my colleague, Dr. Katrina Kamport has done interviews with people who said that they had emotional, really specifically trying to find people who may have regretted
sentences.zh: 现在，你也研究了女性寻求堕胎的原因。

sentences.en: their abortions.
sentences.zh: 最常见的原因有哪些？

sentences.en: And it was very hard to find those people.
sentences.zh: 它们与大多数人认为的原因不同吗？

sentences.en: But when she did, she conducted,
sentences.zh: 嗯，女性堕胎的原因有很多。

sentences.en: I think, 17 interviews.
sentences.zh: 通常，她们选择堕胎的原因不止一个。

sentences.en: And what she found was that it wasn't that people were regretting the abortion itself.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道它们与人们认为的原因有什么不同。

sentences.en: It was that people were regretting the circumstances around the abortion.
sentences.zh: 最常见的原因是财务原因、经济原因，没有合适的经济条件来抚养孩子。

sentences.en: So, this is, there's something that we call decisional regret versus situational regret, which is a term that a colleague of mine, Katie Watson, wrote a paper about.
sentences.zh: 许多女性担心她们现有的孩子，并希望为那个孩子提供比她们当时认为能提供的更好的生活。

sentences.en: And the idea is, in the case of abortion, is that you wish you weren't in that circumstance that led you to need an abortion.
sentences.zh: 有些人因为伴侣相关的原因选择堕胎。

sentences.en: You wish that maybe your partner reacted differently and was more supportive, or you wish that you had better
sentences.zh: 她们没有合适的伴侣。

sentences.en: financial circumstances, or you were, you know, you were more stable housing.
sentences.zh: 是的，原因很多。

sentences.en: There's situations in your life that you wish were different so that you could have that, carry that pregnancy to term.
sentences.zh: 这些原因随着时间的推移发生了变化吗？

sentences.en: And so, there's regret about that.
sentences.zh: 它们往往是人们选择堕胎的相同原因，任何可能导致不适合怀孕和分娩的原因往往就是人们堕胎的原因。

sentences.en: And really, it's very rare that people are regretting that they actually had the abortion once they had no other option.
sentences.zh: 这一点随着时间的推移并没有真正改变。

sentences.en: Now, you've also done research into the reasons why women seek abortions.
sentences.zh: 药物流产的普及在多大程度上改变了现状？

sentences.en: What are some of the most common reasons?
sentences.zh: 与手术流产相比，我们是否看到更多的女性在接受这种治疗？

sentences.en: And do they, do they differ from what most people think?
sentences.zh: 是的，我们看到药物流产的提供量有了巨大的增长。

sentences.en: Well, women have reasons, have abortions for many reasons.

sentences.en: People, the most common reason is financial reasons, economic reasons, not being in the right, having the right financial circumstances to raise a child.

sentences.en: good time to have a carrier pregnancy to term tends to be the reason why people have an abortion.

sentences.en: Are we seeing more women accessing that type of treatment as opposed to surgical abortion?
sentences.zh: 正如我之前提到的，他们更有可能生活在贫困中，很少有人将这些孩子送去收养。

sentences.en: bond with that child.
sentences.zh: 与孩子建立亲密关系。

sentences.zh: 所以我们观察了母婴关系的指标，发现这些指标较低。

sentences.en: And we, um, also saw that, um, that the existing children were less likely to reach those developmental minds,

sentences.en: So the impacts for the children are, are very real.
